subject: Banking
title: Digital Bank Runs
description: A quick, practical guide to Digital Bank Runs.

hook.text: SVB lost $42 billion in one day. Digital banking lets depositors withdraw in seconds.

buildup.text: In the 1930s, lines formed outside banks. Today, withdrawals happen silently through apps.

discovery.text: Social media spreads fear instantly. A viral tweet can trigger panic among millions of depositors simultaneously.

twist.text: A rumor that once needed a street crowd now needs only a group chat, so panic outruns every bottleneck.

climax.text: Technology made deposits mobile but kept regulation static.

punchline.text: Deposits leave in seconds. Regulators respond in days. Speed kills banks.

quiz.question: What makes digital bank runs more dangerous than traditional ones?
options: Deposits can move in seconds, faster than regulators can respond

details.summary: Social media and mobile banking enable bank runs at speeds impossible in the physical world. Silicon Valley Bank lost $42 billion in deposits in a single day, showing how digital tools accelerate financial panic.
details.whyItMatters: Digital bank runs can destroy an institution in hours rather than days.Traditional safeguards like deposit insurance and emergency lending may be too slow to counteract the speed of mobile withdrawals and viral panic.
takeaways: Silicon Valley Bank lost $42 billion in a single day via mobile transfers
Social media amplified panic faster than regulators could respond
Traditional bank run models are outdated for the digital era

faq.question: How fast can a digital bank run happen?
faq.answer: Silicon Valley Bank lost a quarter of its deposits in hours. Customers transferred millions via mobile apps and online banking without needing to physically visit a branch.

faq.question: Can regulators prevent digital bank runs?
faq.answer: Current tools were designed for slower crises. Regulators are exploring faster intervention mechanisms, social media monitoring, and potentially the ability to temporarily pause digital withdrawals during panic, though this raises civil liberty concerns.
